angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 740,921 km at 186.23 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.3698 +/- 0.0103 mas (same row, RUWE 0.90): 186.23 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.065 +/- 0.009 solar radii from Dumusque et al. 2014, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-10 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...789..154D/abstract): 740,921 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.91 +/- 0.021 solar masses from Dumusque et al. 2014, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-10 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...789..154D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5708 +/- 28 K from Dumusque et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-10 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...789..154D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
